text_fidelity_a:
YOSUDA Under Desk Bike Pedal Exerciser for Home/Office Workout - Magnetic Mini Exercise Bike for Arm/Leg Exercise I've owned a bunch of under desk bikes, but I had specific needs when I bought the YOSUDA Under Desk Bike Pedal Exerciser - I wanted a heavier magnetic pedaler with the cranks as close to the front as possible so when pedaling with my arms, I wouldn't have to reach forward. Judging by the videos and pics, this was it.

The YOSUDA has a little rubbing noise - probably the belt - but it's still so quiet that it doesn't wake up my husband in the next room, and it doesn't affect the pedaling motion, which is super smooth. I've owned the MagneTrainer and the DeskCycle, and they're both silent and smooth, but for my arms the YOSUDA has a good crank rotation (8" compared to 10" with the MagneTrainer), and the pedals are much closer to the front than the DeskCycle. The DeskCycle and MagneTrainer are better built than this bike, but it's fine, and I love the handle. I've owned several $50 and under bikes, but there were universally louder and much less smooth than the YOSUDA.

I found the YOSUDA is also good for pedaling using your feet - it sticks to the floor pretty well when used at low resistance, and the pedaling is smooth. If you turn up the resistance, you may have to put it on a rubber mat to keep in in place, but at lower resistance, it stays where you put it.

My only issue about this is that the display is impossible to read in lower light. Since I use it in lower light, and don't care about the metrics, I just use the stop watch function on my phone to keep track of my time.

The YOSUDA Under Desk Bike Pedal Exerciser is pretty much what I expected from the description, the pics and the reviews. Mine has a little rubbing noise when I use it, which I wasn't expecting, but it's super quiet and otherwise IMO this is a very good pedaler for feet and arms. I got it for $125, and it's often on sale for that price or a little less, and for what I paid, I'm giving it back the star I removed for the soft rubbing noise and hard-to-see display, putting it back up to 5 stars. If it was $200 or more, I'd give it 4 stars, but it's a good bike with forward pedals, quiet and smooth operation at a reasonable price, so it gets 5 stars from me.
text_fidelity_b: YOSUDA Under Desk Bike Pedal Exerciser for Home/Office Workout - Magnetic Mini Exercise Bike for Arm/Leg Exercise

My wife thought I was being a bit foolish, but she doesn’t think that anymore! In fact, this Portable Telescopic Stool has only been in the house a bit over 24 hours and we’ve used it half a dozen times! I came up with the idea of a stool when she was nursing her broken foot - it was 5+ months of bed and my needing to help her rehab it - often finding myself kneeling on our floor, which has very hard cement under the carpet - without a carpet pad - so I was hurting. Then there are any number of times one of us ended up needing a stool... but ended up kneeling on the floor or sitting not the floor... So it arrived yesterday and we popped it open - it is really easy. Fingers in the two holes on either end, twist, and pull, twist a little back and it locks in place. We wanted to test the weight - I am a bit heavy still - so I sat on it first. Held me absolute fine. Felt sturdy and safe. But we wanted to really test it - again, I’m a bit heavy right now, so we set it up next to the bed and she stop by me - in case anything went wrong I’d throw myself onto the bed - and up I went - I stood my 200+ body weight on the stool and it worked fine. it stayed in place. I will add: earlier today my wife sat on it for about 20 minutes and did note that it was starting to get a bit uncomfortable. There is no padding - just the plastic - so after awhile she was feeling it. You might be able to rig something to make it more comfortable. But for shorter periods of time it’s fine. Longer and we’ll figure something out - I hope. But overall we are both surprised and thrilled with this Portable Telescopic Stool. It’ll give us the quick stool we’ve needed, and for longer needs, well... we’ll figure something out. But so far, it’s already made a big difference.

This is a thick plastic spork that is just somewhat stronger than a typical plastic utensil. It is BPA-free and is food and dishwasher safe. There is a fork on one end with one of the tines that has a "knife-like" edge. There is a spoon on the other end. The center holes can be used to fasten this to a backpack using the reusable teather it comes packaged with.

I got this because many times when I go on a staycation, I pack a cooler with yogurt and stuff for day travel. This is perfect for that. I ate with the spoon and fork fine but I could not cut anything of substance with the knife. I think $4.99 is reasonable for what this is but the knife-like edge is completely useless. A butter knife cuts better. However, the spoon and fork are good for any "away-type" eating such as camping, backpacking, or just a staycation with a cooler in tow.

Even though the price is right, the reason I give this 3 stars is because the knife is useless and the thick plastic has a different mouth feel and pick-up ability. For instance, when I was eating yogurt with the spoon, I could not scrape the container as easily with the spoon end as I could with the [[ASIN:B07M8K5VQ8 Titanium Spork]]. This is good enough but neither their Titanium spork or this one is great.

I attached two pictures. The first photo is of this set and the second photo is with my Titanium version on the right end for comparison purposes.
text_fidelity_b: UCO Utility Spork 3-in-1 Combo Spoon-Fork-Knife Utensil, 2-Pack, Gold/Sky Blue

text_fidelity_a:
SPRI Step360 Pro Trainer Essentially a marriage between Bosu and regular steppers, this device promises to bring the best of both to the home exercise routine. While it does a provide an acceptable basic workout, it does not quite make the mark.

The device itself is large and bulky. You must inflate it with a really lame hand pump. I thought the pump was flimsy. There are no valves, just holes that are plugged after inflation. Once inflated, it is essentially two firm air cushions topped with a balance board. I did find that it held its air, which was good since I do not relish another round with the hand pump. The enclosed dvd comes with instructions and workouts. If you have resistance bands, you are good to go.If not, you need to purchase some because they are not included. The workouts are basic and unlikely to challenge advanced and intermediate exercisers. Overall, this is not a terribly successful hybrid. There is some wobble but probably not enough to make a significant difference in the workout.

As tempting as this concept was, I did not find it superior to or a replacement for either my regular stepper or Bosu. Although the device itself is sturdy, the cost cutting short cuts (hand pump, no valves, no resistance bands) detract. If you are a beginner with a craving for novelty, this device might be a good choice. But overall, I thought it failed to realize its promise.
text_fidelity_b: SPRI Step360 Pro Trainer

text_fidelity_a:
MAOOY Beach Blanket, 83”X79”Picnic Blanket Beach Mat for 3-7 Adults, Beach Blanket Waterproof Sandproof, Lightweight Portable Picnic Blankets with 4 Stakes for Camping, Travel, Hiking - Quick Drying When I first opened the package my wife wasn’t sure: she said she thought it seemed “cheap” and “like a tarp you can get at Lowes.” But we took it out, opened it a little, and she felt slightly better. But when we took it to the park to give it a try, and laid it out, we were both very happy. This is not as large as another we got (which I think actually that one calls itself extra large), but it is a great size and works well.

The bag it comes in is small, but it works fine and feels like it’s solid for a good number of uses. There are 4 stakes to secure it. When we were out there the wind was picking up and blowing things hard as storms moved through the area. These stakes kept the cover solid on the grass.

It was large enough for two people and supplies. We would use it alone or with the second one for more space - we couldn’t really tell using a measuring tape, so went for both. But this is a good size.

The material is not as cheap as at first appeared. It seems pretty decently solid and like it’ll last for a good while.

The bag is attached to the cover so as not to loose it. A carabiner is included for easily attaching to something for carrying. We had it in a bag for our test day.

We mostly go to the beach rather than parks (Covid has changed that for now) so we didn’t get to test in sand, but we think the stakes, cleaning, and use will be as good. We have been wanting something rather than just our towels to help control bugs and such, and this seems like it can help. (Bugs do whatever they want, but dirt and sand seem like they’ll be easily kept at bay.

We did not do as well repacking - part trying to get out of there before the rain came - but we have to figure out a better method for folding and getting it back in the bag. We got it in, but not all the way - not a big deal overall - but nothing we feel defeats the purpose or lessens the value of the ground cloth.

Overall we are happy with it and plan to use it often, and are happy to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: MAOOY Beach Blanket, 83”X79”Picnic Blanket Beach Mat for 3-7 Adults, Beach Blanket Waterproof Sandproof, Lightweight Portable Picnic Blankets with 4 Stakes for Camping, Travel, Hiking - Quick Drying

Kuat Dirtbag This mount was exactly what I needed. I had built a fork mount roof rack for my fatbike out of an old Thule rack. I originally used a sunlite fatbike fork mount, but after the nut fell off that mount and not being able to buy a new one, I had to replace the whole unit.
I bought the 135mm X 9mm fork mount. This fits fatbike forks with 135mm spacing with quick release. I have. 2014 Specialized fatboy and it fits perfect. It won't fit through axle forks like the Bluto which are 150mm X 15mm. This mount does not come with a 135mm skewer, so you can either buy an extra, or use the one from your wheel. The rear wheels of most mountain bikes is 135mm so they are pretty common and affordable. The fork rests on two short metal tubes the same size as your axle, and just like your axle the skewer goes through the metal tubes to anchor your fork to the mount. This design is ingenious. There has been mention of misalignment in other reviews, mine did not have that problem. If the skewer falls off or someone steals it, you only have to replace the skewer and not the whole unit. This mount is good quality and should last awhile.
text_fidelity_b: Kuat Dirtbag

text_fidelity_a:
AMNQUERXUS Machine Washable Reflective Running Vest with LED Lights USB Rechargeable Safety Gear with Adjustable Waist, High Visibility Light Up Flashing Vest Gifts for Men Women Kids Dog Walking Sometimes where we live, it can get really scary when people drive by quickly and you are trying to go for a walk in the country to just relax. Having this vest handy is really a great item to put on both during the night time or dusk hours, or during hunting season to keep from being shot.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
CLOSURES
This comes with an XL vest that fits around the sides and closes. with strong velcro type closures.

FABRIC
This is a very nice mesh fabric. It allows for airflow and has a slight stretch/give to it so it is comfortable.

SIZING
This fits me and I am between a size 14 and 16 misses. If I were to put this over a winter jacket, I could still close it unless the coat is WAY too puffy.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
POWER BOX
This is ingenious, actually. There is a little packet which recharges. It has a plug on it and also a cord that is USB to recharge it. Once it is charged, then you slip the little box unto a closed pocket which sits under a power button. The box gives a place for the power button to rest on when you press it.

LIGHTS
Once you have it connected, the button is pressed once, and you get the lights on front and back to go on. Once the lights are on, then you can make them flash fast by pressing another time. One more press makes for a slower blink, and a fourth press turns them off.

VEST
The vest itself is brilliant neon yellow. There is plenty of reflective tape all over this vest front and back. There is even a zipper pocket on the front for you to put your phone or other small items in.

BATTERY LIFE?
The battery life of this seems quite good. I have used it a few times and there is still no need for a recharge. I would say you could get a few hours of continuous use at least per charge, maybe more. My outings did not add up to that much yet.

WASHING
I am only going to handwash this without the battery pack and air dry it well before trying to use again. It will dry fast due to the fabric.

HUNTING SEASON
Around my area, fall time into winter can be dangerous. We have had our home shot by hunters by accident, and often there are inexperienced people who try to hunt and they don't pay attention to what is going on, thinking noises are deer. This vest will alert anyone in the early morning or early evening hours that there is a person there.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great vest to have handy. I plan to keep using this especially through hunting season and for late night walks when i hear a car coming.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is an ingenious little invention and I am glad to have it. I am considering purchasing others for the rest of the family.
text_fidelity_b: AMNQUERXUS Machine Washable Reflective Running Vest with LED Lights USB Rechargeable Safety Gear with Adjustable Waist, High Visibility Light Up Flashing Vest Gifts for Men Women Kids Dog Walking

From cheap ones to expensive ones. I always take them apart when I first get them and clean them, add oil where needed and inspect.

At this price, the action on this knife is amazing (see video). While the listing says ceramic bearings these are steel bearings for the pivot (see photos). It is still extremely smooth for deploy and for closing (even though it uses the tiny caged bearings, and they sit directly on the tang without grooves for said caged bearings).

The g10 is nicely textured with just enough checkering, and they are very slim scales which I appreciate as it is a bit bigger for a folder lengthwise. The slim scales give it a great feel and it really is very nice on the pocket and not as noticeable as other knives this length. The clip isn't ambidextrous however (but is tip up) and is right hand carry. It also isn't a deep carry clip but it works well enough (and there are many clips that would work with this 3-screw setup for the pocket clip).

I'm normally not a huge fan of tanto blade shapes but this has the tip grind elongated so that angle on this is much more usable, and looks better in my opinion. It could benefit from some jimping on the spine also, but this is minor.

The lockup is solid, with no wiggle even when getting the blade and pivot to a point where it drops shut.

Really a nice knife overall (and I can sometimes be critical with knives, specifically cheaper knives). At this price point it is really a great value and I'm glad to have received!
text_fidelity_b: Viwki Pocket Folding Knife with 3.34" Blade for Hunting Outdoor Tactical Survival and EDC,Handle w/Embossed Flag, Liner Lock, Flipper Open,Deep Carry Pocketclip

- GOOD ZIPPERS - they're on the left if you're laying in the bag, and they work well without getting caught a lot.
- TWO ZIPPERS - One down the side and one on the bottom. Why is this good? Zippers tend to have issues going around corners, and this seems to help.
- ZIPPER DRAFT TUBE - Huh? They made an extra...insulated tube of fabric next to the zippers running lengthwise that helps keep air out. And it's made of tougher material almost like a backpack which means...drum roll...the zipper finally doesn't get caught on the bag itself!!!
- GOOD HOOD - The hood is really nice and roomy, like put a full size pillow in it roomy. If you sinch it up with the draw string you can have a face-size opening.
- FLEECE FOOT - the inside bottom foot and a half has an extra layer of warm fleece.
- BURROW - I like to kind of burrow down in a sleeping bag and there's so much room you can bend your legs, sleep on your side, have your arm curled under your head, and there's just so much room. I can put my fee at the very bottom and have the opening above my head.
- LOOKS COOL - I know, it's a sleeping bag and how cool do you expect it to look, really? But it really does look pretty cool.

CONS:
- BIG - We put them in stuff sacks that sinch down and they're still pretty big bags.
- NOT FOR BACKPACKING - like everyone says.

HOW TO SLEEP WARMER:
- Put an inexpensive and washable fleece liner inside the bag. There's plenty of room. It adds to the warmth significantly.
- Change your clothes before you sleep. During the day your clothes get moisture from your own body heat. Change before you sleep and not only will you be warmer, having clean clothes inside the bag makes it stay cleaner.
- Don't over-dress. Start off in like shorts and a t-shirt, no socks, and you'll be warm without sweating. If you start off too warm, you'll build up heat, sweat, and then be colder.
- Put your extra layers down in the foot. Got a sweatshirt you'll probably wear in the morning? Shove it down in the foot. There's room, and it'll be warm when you're ready for it in the morning.
- Wear a beanie, helps with heat loss on your head if you stick your head out for fresh air.

FLEECE LINER:
We used something like this (though not this exact one) and it gets even warmer.
https://www.amazon.com/Stansport-Fleece-Sleeping-Bag-Red/dp/B002YXITMW/ref=sr_1_7?dchild=1&keywords=fleece+sleeping+bag+liner&qid=1592870476&sr=8-7

STUFF SACK:
We used a compression stuff sack like this and were able to fit the sleeping bag and the fleece liner in it together.
https://www.amazon.com/Lewis-N-Clark-Compression-Drawstring/dp/B079JRVVD1/ref=sr_1_4?dchild=1&keywords=lewis+n.+clark+compression+sack&qid=1592870350&sr=8-4

text_fidelity_a:
Usitek Fitbit Flex 2 Accessory Bands for Fitbit Flex 2 / Fitbit Flex2,Silicone Fitness Replacement Accessories Wrist Band for 2016 New Fitbit Flex 2 with Steel Buckle,Pack of 3. My husband and I are really happy with these replacement bands (reasons detailed below). Ideally, honestly we would give them a 4.5/5 star rating if possible due to one flaw (lining up of the lights) but otherwise, they are great and we would both recommend!

Look: We got the black, grey, and blue bands and we both really like the colors. Although the black is standard with FitBit Flex2, the dark blue costs extra, so I really like that we can get all three colors here. One thing I can say about the colors though is that the blue band looks much darker in person than on the photo (although, I actually like it better in real life than on the photo). It's not really a big deal, but I think the different color makes it look just a little more professional and a little less like a typical fitness band. And, since there are three bands, you have choice and can change up your band as you change up your outfits!

Feel: I really like how soft the rubber/silicone material is. It is not stiff (as I have found other after market fitness bands to be), nor is it "sticky" (sometimes rubber can catch fine hairs on the arm and feel like it's ripping them out....that is NOT the case with this band!) The clasp on the back is comfortable and doesn't push into the wrist. Overall, it is very soft and comfortable to wear both during the day and at night.

Fit: there are two aspects here- first how the FitBit Flex2 fits into the band and how the band fits on the wrist. The FitBit fits nicely into the "pouch" left for it- it is secure (does not feel like it will fall out) but is not difficult to get it in either. One of my (only) complaints, however, is that the holes on the bands do not line up PERFECTLY with the lights on the FitBit. Honestly, this is such a minor thing and most people might not even notice it at all. I think it's actually largely because the rubber/silicone is a little bit thicker on this band than it is on the normal band, so it looks a little further away, so depending on your angle when you look at it might look like the entire light isn't on (but I have to say you can always tell which light is on or off, it never covers a light or makes it impossible to see- I think I might be slightly anal retentive to even notice!!). As far as the wrist fit goes...I'm actually really impressed here. It fit my husband without a problem and it even fit my (super dainty) wrists in the second to smallest hole! I feel comfortable to say that this would fit (almost) any adult's wrist. There's no need to keep multiple bands around- one size will definitely fit all.

Security and Protection: Although I have never (ever) worried that the clasp on my Fitbit will wear down and I might eventually lose my FitBit, I can see how that might happen (particularly after long periods of wear and removal to charge). Either way, this band removes any slight concern about that fact with the steel (watch like) clasp. It is obvious this clasp will not accidentally loosen and fall off. Ever. I also like that it feels soft and like it will protect my FitBit in case I (inevitably) bang it into something. The band provides enough protection that I won't break it. That being said, one difference between these bands and the band that comes with is the holes (to view the lights) are open on these bands whereas the are covered with a piece of clear plastic on the regular band it comes with. I'm not sure how much protection that clear plastic provides (I tend to find dust and things on the FitBit regardless), but something to mention.

Overall: I would definitely recommend these bands. I think they're high quality- they look and feel really nice on the wrist. And for the price (3 for ~$10) you really cannot lose.
text_fidelity_b: Usitek Fitbit Flex 2 Accessory Bands for Fitbit Flex 2 / Fitbit Flex2,Silicone Fitness Replacement Accessories Wrist Band for 2016 New Fitbit Flex 2 with Steel Buckle,Pack of 3.

text_fidelity_a:
Wake Bike Stem Riser Bike Fork Stem Extender Bicycle Handlebar Raiser Head Up Adapter Suitable for Mountain Bike, Road Bike, MTB, BMX, Fixie (Aluminium Alloy, Adjustable) This WAKE stem riser comes with enough spacer-rings to put your existing handlebar riser at the right height and allow the stem cap and long stem bolt to fully engage. There was a little difficulty in keeping the alignment of the now top and bottom sections of this taller riser assembly, but I found getting the top on first and clamping it in position so the gaps in top and bottom line up vertically is easier than putting the tall riser on first and then aligning and tightening the top section with the handlebars to it. It can be done either way, but it took a lot of fussing, tightening and loosening and twisting. Getting that long bolt in to press the stem cap down to hold everything in position is complicated that the fork bearing will keep everything loose without the correct alignment, so you have to keep that as a goal because nothing can have a final position without that important fork bearing being seated. Then, all you need to do is clamp it all together on the bike. This is a 2 part operation: the long bolt and stem cap forces the assembled units together and down, then clamping the top and bottom riser sections together and to the bike for a solid steering connection. I think this better than the older-style threaded stem which depends on that single bolt to hold everything in place.
-Compressing in several dimensions makes it more secure.-
The test ride, once I was satisfied that everything had been aligned and tightened, was different from how the bike had been only an hour ago. My hands, arms and shoulders were at a more natural angle and riding was much easier. This riser extension is only 2.7 inches, but coupled with the top riser and raised handlebars the difference is more than 8 inches overall. A nice, comfortable ride!
There are youtube videos showing this operation in detail. //// It's important to do it properly! ////

To build muscle, you need to lift weights or otherwise add weight to your body in some way. Dumbbells are a good way to accomplish this and a good option for those who want to lift their weight is this set of Adjustable Dumbbells, from Vivitory.

I’ve used many dumbbells in my day, but this is the first time I have ever had a set that was adjustable. You adjust the weight by removing or adding steel bars and by doing this, you can reduce the weight down to about 5.5 pounds each or even less if you leave off the caps. The maximum weight for each dumbbell is about 18 pounds with all the rods in place. This is enough weight range to make these dumbbells using for many strength- building routines.

Removing and adding the weights to these dumbbells takes time, so don’t go into this thinking it’s going to be quick and simple. It will take effort, but it’s still simple enough that most people wont mind. The reason it takes some effort is because you also have to make sure the pads are in place, otherwise the steel rods will move around while you do your workout.

These dumbbells are easy to grip and they look better than traditional dumbbells, which feature free weights. The colorful appearance is cool, not that this means much for working out, but it does look nicer, less industrial/rugged than the traditional style. And the bars hold in place well- you don’t need to worry that they will fall out while you use the dumbbells.

Strength building is important to those who exercise. A good set of dumbbells can make strength building easier and If you’re the type who doesn’t want to mess with free weights, you might consider this dumbbell set from Vivitory. It’s a good set for those who want a single set of dumbbells for their workout routine.

text_fidelity_a: Gaiam Yoga Duffle Bag The Gaiam Yoga Duffle Bag or DUFFEL BAG, as the label says on the bag itself, is much more attractive in person than in the photos because the sensation of the soft and lightweight fabric enhances the appearance.  I was expecting it to have more pockets, so was surprised to see one inside that also houses a smaller zippered mesh compartment, one on the front of the outside just behind the section that is designed for holding a rolled up yoga mat which also has a small zippered exterior pocket, and one open pocket on both ends, both having a slightly elasticized upper edge.  There is really no hardware to weigh this down, just three light nylon zippers.  This is not designed to carry loads of heavy gear because the two handle straps are simply sewn into the fabric, not reinforced with anything other than the machine stitching, and there is nothing to protect the base of the bag from wear.  Because the fabric is lightweight and easy to clean, it is also crushable, so it is a good option to take with you for travel inside another suitcase for excess gear upon your return.  As for its intended purpose as a yoga bag, I find that by putting my mat inside a nylon bag I received with another yoga backpack, I can more easily slide it into the carrying spot in this bag.  The photos of this product appear very similar to the Gaiam Metro bag, which also is rather inviting.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Yoga Duffle Bag

My former 2-hold belt buckle of iron lasted over 20 years - till stolen (another story).

text_fidelity_a: East West U.S.A D3031 31" Sports Duffle Gym Travel Gear Bag My first impression... it is much lower quality than I was expecting.  At 31 inches long it has ample and generous storage, but the zippers tended to snag, and the fabric and overall quality was lower than I'd expect for a bag in the 30 dollar range.  I paid much much less than that so I'm not too disappointed. If I was to fill the bag full with moderate weight items I don't think the bag would hold up long.  It has a lot of space, I'd estimate it could over the SHORT-term maybe handle up to 50 pounds. With a bag this size you could easily reach that weight.  On the other hand, this bag will work awesome for lightweight bulky objects, I could see myself throwing a rolled yoga mat, a couple towels, change of clothes, pair of shoes, and a bunch of other stuff in it and still have some room.  I'd be hesitant to use this as luggage although maybe it would work for just for car trips.  I think it will work great for storing bulky comforters or blankets for the summer.  Most of the 31 inch length is the main compartment and the zippered opening opens big and wide.  The end compartments each take up only a few inches of the full length. Again I was very impressed with the large size. It appears much larger in person than the picture. If it's stuffed full the proportions will probably be similar to what's pictured.
text_fidelity_b: East West U.S.A D3031 31" Sports Duffle Gym Travel Gear Bag

Planet Bike Beamer 3 Bike Headlight This light has two practical safety functions:

It helps make your presence on the road more apparent to on coming traffic. The light is bright enough from even a few hundred feet that a driver would have to be extremely oblivious and distracted not to see it.

Perhaps more importantly, the light will illuminate street signs and signals that are made with a reflective material at distances of over 450 feet away (I measured using google maps). When I first used the light (in flashing mode), I was genuinely shocked to see how the street signs up to two blocks ahead of me were pulsating. I say that this is important because it helps you spot stop signs in the distance - assuming you're being a safe cyclist, biking in a lane, with traffic, abiding by traffic laws, you're probably most likely to get killed by accidently running a stop sign. When I bike home from work at night, I take streets that have no traffic lights and only stop signs, so being able to spot them is very important for me.

The light attaches to your handle bar through via a mount; the light can easily slid off the mount so you don't have to bike around with it during the day, nor leave it on the bike when it's parked outside.

The light does what it needs to do for a reasonable price. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
Ridge Runner Brimstone Canyon Machete/Fixed Blade Knife with Nylon Sheath I am a knife collector who also buys knives as tools to use while trimming mangroves and removing invasive vegetation from the wetlands on our property in Southwest Florida. Twice a year I find myself in the wetlands trimming away so that we can maintain our water view as per current regulations in place. Because of the hazardous footing, thick vegetation, and dangerous flora and fauna -- I primarily use machetes and hatchets for my work. I want to be able to see and hear any of the frequent obstacles I encounter daily in that dangerous mess.

The average width of the limbs I am currently trimming require a short chopping motion since the trees are so tightly packed together. I usually depend on an Esee Lite Machete for most of the work but it is too long and requires swinging it to be most effective, hence my serch for a good chopper. This Ridge Runner Brimstone Canyon Machete fits the bill. It is well built with a full taexng ending in a butt plate. The blade is a full 12" of 440 stainless steel and it has a pommel to help protect your swinging hand.

It arrived sharp enough to shave hair off my arm and to pass the paper test. The cutting side is thin and curved with the top of the blade carrying the weight for more effective chopping. It even has several serrations at the top of the blade for cutting/sawing. The pakkawood handle is fastened to the full tang blade with three bolts and the machete itself has a nice solid feel. The handle is a bit small and slippery for me but that is easily remedied with grip tape and gloves.

Here's the kicker. Some people might collect this type of knife because it is well assembled, visually appealing, and feelsgood in the hand. However I bought this as a working tool for a very reasonable price and feel that it offers considerable value for the cost. Looking for an effective chopper? Search no more. And by the way, it comes with a black nylon sheath that should last as long as it is properly used and cared for.
text_fidelity_b: Ridge Runner Brimstone Canyon Machete/Fixed Blade Knife with Nylon Sheath

text_fidelity_a:
Atlas 2008 Women's Elektra 11 Series Snowshoe I am adding this paragraph after three trips. The bindings have lots of rivets, and
I wondered about their durability. After the third trip, when I took off the shoes,
one of the rivets holding the heel strap broke. Fortunately I was back at the car;
if some of the rivets fail out on the trail, the shoe could become useless. Other
reviews that I have seen have not mentioned a problem with durability, but now I
wonder. The rest of the review hasn't changed.

This snowshoe has lots of good points. The only negative, and the reason that I did
not give it 5 stars, is a lack of flotation. I cannot compare it to other snowshoes
of the "modern" solid decking type, or the "traditional" wood frame lattice decking,
though it seems to have less flotation than my traditional shoes. I got the 27"
model, and with pack I weigh under 165 lbs; the shoes are rated to 200 lbs or more.
In a soft, old snow, I sank in 8-12" breaking trail; sometimes I sank in more.

The shoe has some very good points. The bindings are secure and comfortable, and
they won't ruin your leather boots or give you blisters by clamping down on the top
of your toes. The traction is good. The toes snap up automatically, and you can walk
with a pretty normal stride. Because of the short distance between your toes and
the toes of the shoes, the lack of a long tail, and the crampons, you can climb
over deadfall very easily. There's no need to back up to free your toes, burying
your tail in the process. I like the heel lift, though I only tried it briefly.
The lift bars are very stiff to put back down. The shoes are lightweight and don't
carry lots of snow on their tops, so you don't have to lift lots of weight with
each step. The natural stride and light weight tend to offset the less than ideal
flotation.

Pros:
Excellent binding system, excellent or very good traction, very good walking
stride, light weight

Cons:
Flotation may be somewhat lacking - I can't compare to other shoes, just to an
ideal, which is not possible to achieve
text_fidelity_b: Atlas 2008 Women's Elektra 11 Series Snowshoe

text_fidelity_a:
Retrospec Solstice Trekking & Ski Poles for Men & Women - Aluminum w/Cork or Foam Grip - Adjustable & Collapsible Lightweight Hiking, Walking & Skiing Sticks Good light, sturdy poles. They aren't cheap feeling. I am really quite impressed with the design, how they feel, and the overall options included. They come clipped together (keep the clips, or discard) tucked away in a nylon drawstring storage bag. The kit contains wide and narrow snow baskets and rubber boots/tip. Just screw on. Can choose to use none of those and just use the carbide tip. Can elongate both portions via a clip to your height needs. I am 5'10" and these are plenty long for me. They shorten down to manageable height for easy storage and carry. The carry bag has a shoulder strap.

I have used these for snow shoeing, XC/alpine skiing (not nordic/down hill- these are not meant for that), walking through snow in regular boots, walking in mixed dirt/snow/ice. They are really quite sturdy. They are way better than a pair of basic walking pole/sticks I had that broke on a trail within a couple of uses. I find the ones that are capable for snow use to be better. These are better priced than many too. I would/will recommend these!

My primary use though: I happen to have a long semi steep hill directly outside my back door. We have dogs, so we are always going down that hill to get to more leveled out ground. The soil is sandy and doesn't hold grass well. So we are missing a lot of grass and even where there is grass, it tends to get kicked up easily. So even on dry days it can be a slipping hazard. Now add in rain, mud, ice, snow.. and well you can understand what I am about to say next: trekking poles (and good boots) help. Use of poles add a little additional stability. I like to use mine with the large cups, for this purpose. Our winter thus far in NY has been pretty much spring like. Not enough snow to keep mud/ice at bay, not enough cold to keep things firmed up out there. I want my freezing days, and we have barely had any. No Almost no reprieve from mud and slop. So much potential slippage. So much dirty paw action! Ah well.

Bright spot is getting out to play with my dogs and using these to walk around the yard. I just use them for the hill, but once down to the level area, I mind as well keep on using them.. so in this sense I am getting an additional work out of the sort because I am using my arms to move these. I will continue to use these come spring/summer on my walks for that very reason (which is why I had walking sticks before.. for additional burn)

The product description did a great job describing these and the included pictures are spot on. I included a pics of my dogs on the hill. We aren't even to the bottom yet. You can see a little bit of the back of the house at top of hill. You see that the hill starts immediately. Many people have asked if we go sledding on this hill. At bottom of hill the land levels out for maybe 20 feet and butts up to a creek. The back yard is an adventurous place!-- and these multi use trekking poles are helping me navigate it in a more safe and steady manner. Yay!
text_fidelity_b: Retrospec Solstice Trekking & Ski Poles for Men & Women - Aluminum w/Cork or Foam Grip - Adjustable & Collapsible Lightweight Hiking, Walking & Skiing Sticks

The colors are vivid. It has some basic hanging hardware included, but no cabinet. You can get by without a cabinet if you mount a piece of plywood or something similar behind the dart board, or if you just don't care about getting holes punched in your wall. I suggest looking up regulation height and distance to mount the board if you want the best experience playing.

The six darts that are included are perfectly adequate for getting started; there are two different fin designs to help differentiate between two players' darts. The darts are not amazing by any means, and you'll likely want to get better ones if you really enjoy the game. They don't have the best grips, and they aren't very fancy or anything, but they fly true as far as I can tell, their points are very sharp, and they should do just fine.

text_fidelity_a:
Alloy Car Roof Bike Bicycle Fork Mount Carrier Rack Max Load 44 lbs After reading the pros and cons of fork-mounting vs upright (wheel-mount) I decided to go with these, figuring the mostly aluminum structure would last a while and the fork-mounting would secure the bikes well. I've used the product one time on a short trip, but so far it seems sturdy and the bikes are locked on firmly. My one concern, which I knew in advance of purchase, is that the fork mount only holds the traditional thin skewers/axles. That works fine for our family fleet of tourers and hybrids from years 1998 through about 2012. However, a lot of new bikes now have the much fatter through-axles (particularly bikes w/ disc brakes). So if i get a new bike I'll probably need a new rack.

Vehicle: 2016 Subaru Outback

Pros:
-My big Cannondale Adventure 400 and my wife's Giant Sedona fit perfectly and are secured with front quick release and included rear hold-down strap.
-Reasonable price, though not as inexpensive as some all-steel models out there.
-No tools required, no customization needed for our Outback with factory folding roof rack.
-Seems and looks solid for those worried about appearance.

Cons:
-May need to fiddle with how many spacers to use with each bolt. There are six bolts on each rack.
-Installation, certainly the first time, might take up to 20 minutes for each rack. And sometimes it's hard to get those big wingnuts to thread properly given the awkward angle since the bolt is vertical and you may not have much space to install the wingnut between bolt and roof of car.
-Very easy to have the spacers fall off the bolts before wingnut is threaded. I had two or three roll off the back of our vehicle. No biggie on a flat concrete driveway but can be a problem on gravel or camping.
-It doesn't lock, which is okay for our needs. I can probably run a cable lock through the frame/tires and part of our roof rack. This may not keep the racks from being stolen but it would be a real pain to remove with bikes mounted. -Of course, it's nice to leave the rack on all summer if you use it frequently, but note someone can get a rack off in 3 minutes if there's no bike on it.
-For any roof rack, it may take a little strength and height to put the bike on top of a car/SUV and simultaneously align that front fork with the locking axle (built into the rack). I'm over 6 feet but my wife is 5'-6" - no way can she use this rack w/ her hybrid. Might be different w/ an ultra-light tourer and a foot stool.
text_fidelity_b: Alloy Car Roof Bike Bicycle Fork Mount Carrier Rack Max Load 44 lbs

text_fidelity_a:
Schwinn Gammon Men's 18 Cruiser Bicycle, 18-Inch/Medium, Black, 18"/Medium 1999 was the last time I actually owned a bicycle. When I saw this one, it struck a chord of nostalgia in me so I thought I ought to give casual biking another try. This is a very casual, suburbia type bike. No bells (literally no bell) and no frills or fancy gears to mess with. It's meant for just tooling along in a relaxed manner on shady, wide, well paved, low traffic neighborhood streets. I'll be honest, I have never understood or cared about the difference between men's and women's bikes - frankly, that lowered center bar on women's bikes always seemed like it would be the safer option for a man to me.

This has to be assembled when it arrives and that drives me nuts. The box is enormous and already weighs over 70lbs. Sending it fully assembled couldn't possibly be significantly more difficult and it would definitely be easier on the customer. This thing requires multiple hex wrenches and regular wrenches to put together and if you've never done it before, it's complicated. I ended up having to get a friend to help me out because some of the bolts were torqued so tight that I couldn't undo them to attach the handle bars. (Someone with previous bike building experience might not experience the frustrations that I did) We ended up leaving off the front fender because it bent and dented when I tried to install by myself.

Actually riding this bike is fine. It's nicely balanced and the tires are wide enough that I don't feel like I'm teetering around. It travels smoothly down paved neighborhood streets and paved bike trails in our city parks. There are no handle bar brakes though, you have to push the pedals back to brake - I've forgotten how to do that smoothly in the past 20 years and bounced myself off this bike twice already. Nonetheless, I'm enjoying the bike and having fun with it.
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Gammon Men's 18 Cruiser Bicycle, 18-Inch/Medium, Black, 18"/Medium

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Versa 3 Health & Fitness Smartwatch with GPS, 24/7 Heart Rate, Alexa Built-in, 6+ Days Battery, Black/Black, One Size (S & L Bands Included) Now that I have used this Fitbit for a few weeks I feel like I have an idea about it. I've wanted a Fitbit for years, I've heard nothing but amazing things about it and how great they are. Well, to be honest, I am not seeing the greatness of them now that I actually have one. Maybe it's because this is the newest one, maybe there are still bugs to fix, and maybe it could be my phone that just hates everything about the Fitbit app. Honestly, I don't know but either way, I am so unimpressed with this Fitbit.

The pros I have found out is that it was easy to set up and make an account with Fitbit. Everything downloaded, updated, and whatever else perfectly. It was easy to change all the settings and personalize everything the way I wanted it. I love that you can customize the face so that it matches your personality or the types of apps or stuff you want it to show first right on the face. I like that you can control your music and pay for your watch too. Those are great ideas and honestly if I got out more and whatever else I can see where tons of people would totally get so much use out of it.

My biggest beef I have with this though is the fact that I wear it constantly and I want to keep up mainly with my steps, how much I move, and my sleeping patterns. It doesn't have any problems keeping up with all of that and so much more. The problem I have with this watch is the fact that it disconnects from the wifi and then becomes difficult to sync to the app, if at all. I've already had to reset to factory settings once to get it to reconnect to the app, which also has its own set of challenges because once the watch goes the app doesn't want to do much either. I can't remove the watch to re-add it in the app and I'm unable to view the wifi connections to change them or re-add them. It's like everything stops and becomes completely unusable. It's a real pain, to say the least.

Adjustable Back Exercise Ball Office Chair - Standard or (Exclusive)"Tall Boy" Frame Height - with 52cm Ball - Office size 60mm/2.5" wheels - w/Starter Pump and Ball Measuring Tape Very well designed chair. Very excellent value for people with back problems. At this price point you have to take a flyer with this chair if you have back issues!

My specific back issues allow me to sit in the chair for only a few hours. I let my chiropractor borrow the chair for a few days. Folks in the office either liked it or didn't.

I'm 6 feet. I definitely needed the accessory leg lift kit.

Two small issues:
1) The nuts that keep the metal retainer bar in place dig into fairly soft plastic and the torquing of the chair in use works the nuts loose. I'm always finding a nut on the floor and I have to re-tighten. Need to add a lock washer and firm up the plastic the nut interfaces to.

2) Two wheels come with locking mechanisms. No matter where you put these wheels you end up locking the wheels somehow. A couple Amazon reviewers recommend using the two back wheels, but I still lock one or the other. If you use the back wheels, then if you don't remember to check for locked when you sit down, then when you get up you will knock the chair over backwards since the chair is so light.

I found a workaround to #2. I Took pliers and twisted off the tab that controls the locking mechanism, then used a knife to shave off the locking lever plastic, to make sure shoes, etc. don't snag and lock the wheels. The locking mechanism still works fine, but now I have to use my fingernail to flip the lever. Problem solved!

I would definitely recommend you try this chair!
text_fidelity_b: Isokinetics Inc. Adjustable Back Exercise Ball Office Chair - Standard or (Exclusive)"Tall Boy" Frame Height - with 52cm Ball - Office size 60mm/2.5" wheels - w/Starter Pump and Ball Measuring Tape
